messages.text: Our dad died and left the house in his will. My sister A wants to buy it with her husband at a "family discount". I'm not signing off on that. Our younger sister B could use some money too. Can you help us sort this out?

Thanks. I want the house handled fairly, and I want a fair financial share. I haven’t agreed to A’s discounted buy-out, and I won’t subsidize it. B should be able to use her own share, though I can’t set the amount or terms. I want to be able to say no without pressure, and I’m not in a hurry. Your wording about freely saying yes or no with clear information and no pressure fits.

I’d like to buy the house with my husband because owning it would give me more financial independence. A family discount matters to making that possible, though no price is settled. The house means a lot because it’s our family home, and I want us to decide without pressure; C’s agreement matters, and I don’t know why she’s reluctant. I know B wants money, but not what for. Your wording fits.

Thank you. The house matters, but I don’t have a particular plan for it yet. I’d like some money to start a dance studio; that’s the only way I can see moving forward. Your wording about everyone being able to say yes or no freely fits for me.

1–5 fit. By “fair,” I mean my financial share should be respected, and I shouldn’t bear the cost of A getting a discount. That matters to me because I want a fair outcome without subsidizing her. B should speak for herself, and that wording fits. I’m not in a hurry, but I want room to decline without pressure. I want to be fair to A without giving up my own fair share. Your shared wording fits too.

1–4 fit. Financial independence matters to me because I want to stand on my own financially. A lower price matters because it would make buying the house more affordable for me. The house is our family home, so treating it with care matters. I want decisions made without pressure, and C’s genuine agreement is necessary to proceed. Your statement about each sister speaking for herself fits too, as does the shared statement.

1. Not quite—I care about the house, but I’m not sure what it means to us or what should happen to it.  
2. Yes. I don’t want to be rushed into deciding.  
3. I’d say, “I want my dance work and ambitions to be taken seriously.” I care about it because starting a studio is the only way I can see moving forward, and I need money to do that.  
4. I’m not sure what “on my own terms” means here.  
Your statement about each sister speaking for herself fits. The statement about freely saying yes or no still fits too.

“I want the house treated with care while I’m still making up my mind” fits. Being described by me and taken into account feels covered by each sister speaking for herself. “I want to have the means to move forward with my dance work” fits too. I don’t think I’ve held back, but I’d like us to go slowly.

The wording about going slowly fits. I’m not sure about the will statement—I’d want to understand what it says, but I don’t know enough to confirm that wording. I haven’t held anything back, and I don’t have anything else to add right now.

I haven’t held anything back because C contacted you. Her agreement matters because we can’t proceed without it, and I don’t know why she’s reluctant. I want to understand what the will says about who’s included; I don’t know its wording, and I don’t assume it includes my husband. The shared wording about clear understanding of the will fits. Going slowly enough to keep everyone’s needs visible fits too; I don’t want anyone pressured. I have no discomfort with the list as I understand it.

A’s interests should be treated fairly too; I care about her, but not at the cost of my fair share. Going slowly is fine—I’m not in a hurry. I want us to understand what the will says before weighing plans, though I don’t know its terms. I’m wary of A’s husband being involved, but that isn’t the only reason I haven’t agreed to the discount. I have no other wording discomfort.
